solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Excitement about vaguely hot relative, 18

definitions.note: the cross-reference points to the answer of 18-down, a proposition to be proved

indicators.note: the excitement word wraps around the jumbled letters, as 'about' means surrounding

parts.note: hype is excited publicity or fuss

indicators.note: something done vaguely is imprecise, so the letters of hot are loosely rearranged

parts.note: a sister, shortened to sis, is a relative

explanation.surface: Someone gets excited about a vaguely attractive relative, with a cross-reference tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is only a number: it points to the answer of 18-down, which means the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a proposition put forward for testing or proof, so the cross-referenced light serves as a loose synonym.

clue.text: Big cheese and nut

definitions.meaning: a boss or most important person
slang for the human skull or top of the body

explanation.surface: A shopping list item: a large cheese and some nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief is a big cheese, and nut is slang for the cranium, both senses of the same short word.

clue.text: Person who hangs father for a monarch?

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
per means for each, as in 'a pound per item'
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A grim question about someone who would execute their own father on behalf of a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person who hangs' suggests an executioner, but the hanging is of wallpaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorator who puts up wallpaper is said to hang it, so the definition describes the trade by its main action.

clue.text: Change pair of trousers with dirt found in a state

indicators.note: a pair is two, so the first two letters of trousers are taken
the dirt is located inside the state word

parts.note: a nation is a state
smut is dirt or soot

explanation.surface: Someone swaps a pair of trousers that have got grubby, leaving them in a terrible state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pair of' means the first two letters of 'trousers', not a garment; 'found in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Transmutation is a transformation from one form into another, so it is a noun synonym for a change.

clue.text: Final city turned up supporting opening in Brussels

indicators.note: in a down clue, a supporting piece sits beneath the rest
the opening word sits within the letters standing for Brussels

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the EU, so it stands for those letters
a vent is an opening or outlet

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the city's letters from the bottom upwards

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is the usual crossword city

explanation.surface: The last city on a tour rises in support of a new opening in Brussels.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'turned up' reads the city from the bottom, and 'supporting' places that piece underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventual means coming at the end of a process, so it is an adjectival synonym for final.

clue.text: Enter Russian leader, cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round from one end of the name to the other

parts.note: Vladimir Putin is the Russian president

explanation.surface: A command that the Russian president should come in riding a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves the final IN of PUTIN to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To input data is to key it in, a computing synonym for enter as a verb.

clue.text: Trap one somewhere dry

parts.note: trap and gob are both slang for the mouth
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Catching a lone animal in an arid place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trap' looks like a verb but is slang for the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a vast desert in Mongolia and China, an example of an arid place.

clue.text: Shock right during time with no power

indicators.note: the right letter falls within the power-cut word

parts.note: an outage is a period when the electricity supply fails

explanation.surface: An electric shock happens just as the power goes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrage is a strong feeling of shocked anger; as a verb it means to shock or offend deeply.

clue.text: Bishop punching two volunteers can start to get tiresome

indicators.note: the bishop's letters punch through into the middle of the numeral

parts.note: II is the Roman numeral two
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop
the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force
a tin is a can

indicators.note: the start of the word get is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A churchman assaulting a couple of helpers soon becomes wearisome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two' is a Roman numeral, not a count of volunteers; 'punching' is the container signal and 'start to' takes an initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irritating is annoying or wearing, so it is a fair synonym for tiresome.

clue.text: A mountain has no sun

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

indicators.note: with no means without, so the sun letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written before the deletion
S abbreviates Sunday, the sun-day

explanation.surface: A mountain is so high it never sees the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' drops S from HAS. 'A' looks like the article but is the definition: alpha is the Greek letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet, equivalent to the Roman letter at the start of ours.

clue.text: One facilitating export almost died at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so the letters are muddled
almost the whole word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before being cut short

explanation.surface: An exporter's agent perishes during a sea voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims DIED to DIE, and 'at sea' rearranges EXPORT plus DIE.
explanation.definitionFit: An expeditor speeds up or eases a process, so it is someone who makes things easier to achieve.

clue.text: Fabulously attired to take somebody out?

definitions.meaning: read playfully, dressed for taking a date out; the question mark flags the whimsy

explanation.surface: Someone is dressed glamorously for an evening out with a date.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means dressed to impress, and the second reading puns on 'take out' with its darker slang sense.

clue.text: Fall into a trap? Quite the opposite

definitions.text: Fall into a trap? Quite the opposite

parts.words: Fall into a trap? Quite the opposite
parts.note: the idiom for falling for a provocation uses an upward verb, the opposite of falling

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark that someone has done the reverse of getting caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means exactly to fall into a trap, but its first word is the opposite of fall, which is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to react to a provocation as intended, like a fish taking a lure, so it is being caught out.

clue.text: Hack exposed lunatic predicted to get rid of first official

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its outer covering, so the outer letters go
lunatic suggests craziness, so the remaining letters are jumbled
the opening letter of predicted is discarded

parts.note: taken as written before the deletion

explanation.surface: A journalist reveals that a crazy forecast got a senior figure sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' strips HACK to AC; 'to get rid of first' drops P from PREDICTED, and 'lunatic' rearranges REDICTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Accredited means officially recognised or authorised, so it is an adjectival synonym for official.

clue.text: I arc and curl around, being this

definitions.text: I arc and curl around, being this

indicators.note: moving the letters around rearranges them, as well as describing a looping shape

explanation.surface: A shape speaks: it bends and loops round, which makes it what it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges I ARC and CURL; the whole clue describes the answer, as something arcing and curling round is round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that arcs and curls back round to its start forms a ring shape, which is the meaning of the answer.

clue.text: Permission to insist upon getting king to become knight

indicators.note: one letter turns into another, so the king letter is replaced

parts.note: to assert something is to insist upon it
R abbreviates rex, Latin for king
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A chess player gets permission to promote a king into a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become' swaps the R of ASSERT for N.
explanation.definitionFit: Assent is agreement or approval, as in royal assent, so it means permission granted.

clue.text: Unpleasant broadcast flourished to an extent

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard, so the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: a plant that flourished grew
some means partly, as in 'it helped some'

explanation.surface: Something unpleasant on the airwaves did quite well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns GREW into the sound-alike GRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome means horrible and repellent, a stronger synonym for unpleasant.

clue.text: Knock sailor getting capsized by rubbish

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, so the sailor's letters are turned round

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
tat is shoddy rubbish

explanation.surface: A sailor knocked over and capsized by a load of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsized' reverses TAR into RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated word imitates a rapping at a door, so it names a knock.

clue.text: Proposition unlikely hero having met up outside

indicators.note: the reversed word sits round the jumbled letters
in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top
an unlikely arrangement is a strange one, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An improbable hero has a romantic proposition after meeting someone.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses the word; 'unlikely' is the anagram signal and 'outside' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a mathematical statement to be proved, a formal kind of proposition.

clue.text: Game in which answers are entered by press?

parts.note: a crossword's answers go into the grid
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: A newspaper puzzle whose answers are printed by the press.
explanation.walkthrough: Gridiron is a name for American football, from the lines marked on the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Gridiron is another name for American football, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: Call about oxygen lines being subject to regular review

indicators.note: the call word goes about, or around, the other letters

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
L is a line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: A phone call about oxygen supply lines that are checked routinely.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolling plan or contract is renewed or revised at set intervals, so it is continually reviewed.

clue.text: Hardened criminal with old doyen swallows Ecstasy

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in the drug letter
a criminal arrangement is a wrong one, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A hardened crook and an elderly grandee take a dose of ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges WITH OLD DOYEN into DYEDINTHWOOL, and 'swallows' puts E inside, before WOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyed-in-the-wool means firmly fixed in one's views, an idiom for hardened or inveterate.

clue.text: One attempts run during row

indicators.note: the run letter falls within the row word

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
R abbreviates run, as in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: Someone has a go at a run in the middle of an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but here it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A trier is a person who tries, so 'one attempts' names that person, reading 'attempts' as a verb with one as its subject.

clue.text: Forget love with German

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
mit is German for with

explanation.surface: A plea to forget a German lover.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to leave it out, which is what forgetting it does.

clue.text: Director cheers tirade about abandoning pie-eyed icon

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
a rant is a tirade

indicators.note: pie-eyed means drunk, so the remaining letters stagger into a new order
the letter for about is left out of icon

parts.note: taken as written before the deletion
C abbreviates circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A film-maker cheers a drunken rant about a famous figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' drops C from ICON, and 'pie-eyed' rearranges ION into INO.
explanation.definitionFit: Quentin Tarantino is the American film director of Pulp Fiction, an example of a director.

clue.text: Expression of love in south of France that's taken the wrong way

indicators.note: read the wrong way, the letters run backwards
the love letter goes into the region name

parts.note: the Midi is the south of France
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A declaration of love in Provence that is misunderstood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside MIDI to give MOIDI, and 'taken the wrong way' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a set phrase whose meaning differs from its words, a kind of expression.

clue.text: Get rid of what's slung back by page

indicators.note: back means the letters run in reverse

parts.note: in mud-slinging, mud is what gets thrown

explanation.surface: A page boy disposes of what is thrown back at him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses MUD into DUM.
explanation.definitionFit: To dump something is to discard it, a verb synonym for getting rid of.

clue.text: Something to make one go?

parts.note: a traffic signal that tells drivers to proceed, and also a figure for approval

explanation.definitionFit: A traffic signal of this colour tells drivers to proceed, and figuratively it is permission to start a project.
